builders.angle: LITERAL -- the angle that won rounds 20, 23-25 and 29. Work BRIEF-r34's fix list 1 to 3 in order and exactly as written, one wing at a time, the Hedge Maze FIRST (the lowest-scored room in the house, top of both judges' headroom lists). Keep every change inside your four wings.

THE NEAR FLOOR FIRST -- both judges' first shared defect, and the angle that won round 31 (HEMATITE). Take round 31's near-floor mechanism (runner or flags, a lamp pool, near props above the hand's edge), carry it into your four wings, prove it there, then sweep all seventeen SEEDED and keep it only where it lifts a room; then each wing's own defect in that light.

THE SILHOUETTE DRAWN, NOT TEXTURED. Each wing's worst thing is a box wearing a texture: the hedge's ruler-straight top, the Foyer's flat grey edge slabs, the Greenhouse's blown smear over thin beds, the Kennels' blurred stall band. Draw each as a real object with a broken, inked silhouette first -- leaf mass with a ragged top and dark base, carved jambs and a lintel, dense fronds at several heights, crisp boards and gates -- then dress and light the near floor.
